conflicts.point: Whether continuous integration and decentralized patching are sufficient to manage AI safety risks compared to pre-market regulatory reviews.

positions.stance: Argues that continuous integration and decentralized bug-bounty markets provide faster and more adaptable safety convergence than static pre-market audits.
Argues that complex models exhibit unverified generalization boundaries that require absolute structural barriers and pre-market certification before deployment.

conflicts.point: Whether AI oversight policy should prioritize mitigating speculative long-term existential risks or addressing documented near-term harms such as algorithmic discrimination and resource extraction.

positions.stance: Argues that regulatory focus should center on auditing data center resource use and enforcing civil rights constraints on deployed systems rather than managing hypothetical superintelligence.
Argues that failing to institute strict pre-market controls for advanced models risks unrecoverable systemic collapse.

verdicts.conflict: Whether continuous integration and decentralized patching are sufficient to manage AI safety risks compared to pre-market regulatory reviews.
verdicts.rationale: Safety advocates provide stronger empirical evidence by documenting specific out-of-distribution generalization failures in high-parameter models. Accelerationists rely primarily on analogies to traditional software development that ignore the statistical opacity unique to neural networks.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Demonstrating that decentralized bug-bounty markets and automated validation loops can reliably catch catastrophic failure modes in frontier models before deployment would reverse this finding.

verdicts.conflict: Whether AI oversight policy should prioritize mitigating speculative long-term existential risks or addressing documented near-term harms such as algorithmic discrimination and resource extraction.
verdicts.rationale: Skeptics and safety advocates address entirely different domains of harm without intersecting on a shared metric of severity. Resolving this requires a normative value judgment about whether to prioritize preventative existential security or immediate material remediation.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Establishing an empirical baseline that proves either that advanced alignment failures are imminent or that current near-term extraction harms outweigh speculative risks would tip the balance.
